title: Signed totalization of the perfect formula
statement:
For a bounded finite-projective complex $F^\bullet$, the total arrows
$\pi_{h,E,F}$ and $\rho_{h,E,F}$ are inverse isomorphisms.

proof.text: Use the morphism $h$ and object $E$ of [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows], writing $R$ and $S$ for the coefficient ring sheaves on its target and source. Work on the localization on which the displayed strict-perfect package is given. Choose a K-injective representative $I$ of $E$ using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]; smallness is in the chosen site universe, not a finiteness assumption on the topos. Put $A=h_*I$. An additive functor on complexes sends shifts and cone matrices to the corresponding shifts and cone matrices, hence $Qh_*$ is exact on homotopy categories. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] identifies $QA$ with $Rh_*E$. Each $F^r$ is a retract of a finite free sheaf, so tensoring with it is a retract of a finite power of the identity; it is exact. The same splitting after $h^*$ shows that $h^*F^r$ is flat over $S$. By [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site], $F$ is K-flat; [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] says $h^*F$ is K-flat and represents $Lh^*F$. Tensoring a quasi-isomorphism with a K-flat complex preserves it: its cone is the tensor of the acyclic original cone, with the cone signs identified by the total differential. Thus $C=\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes_R F)$ represents $Rh_*E\otimes_R^L F$. By [lem-weil-pbc-split-perfect-tensor-kinjective], $J=\operatorname{Tot}(I\otimes_S h^*F)$ is K-injective, so $B=h_*J$ represents $Rh_*(E\otimes_S^L Lh^*F)$ by the same total-derived computation. In degree $n$ the sums over $a+r=n$ are finite because $F$ is bounded, even when $I$ is unbounded; $h_*$ preserves these sums since finite sums of modules are finite products and a right adjoint preserves products.

proof.text: At bidegree $(a,r)$ let $t_{a,r}:h_*I^a\otimes_R F^r\to h_*(I^a\otimes_S h^*F^r)$ be the ordinary adjunct of $\varepsilon_{I^a}\otimes1$, with the ordinary pullback-tensor identification. Using the module-pullback definition in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], this identification follows from $h^*M=S\otimes_{h^{-1}R}h^{-1}M$: on local tensors its inverse sends $(s\otimes m)\otimes(s'\otimes f)$ to $ss'\otimes(m\otimes f)$ and its forward map sends $s\otimes(m\otimes f)$ to $(s\otimes m)\otimes(1\otimes f)$. The balanced relations make these inverse maps. For a finite free term $R^N$, this is precisely the identification $(h_*I^a)^N\to h_*((I^a)^N)$: its composites with all $N$ coordinate projections are the identity adjuncts. Write $q_{a,N}$ for its inverse. For the package splitting put $s_{a,r}=(1\otimes p_r)q_{a,N_r}h_*(1\otimes h^*i_r)$. Naturality of the ordinary counit gives $h_*(1\otimes h^*i_r)t_{a,r}=t_{a,N_r}(1\otimes i_r)$ and $h_*(1\otimes h^*p_r)t_{a,N_r}=t_{a,r}(1\otimes p_r)$. Substitution and $p_ri_r=1$ give $s_{a,r}t_{a,r}=(1\otimes p_r)q_{a,N_r}t_{a,N_r}(1\otimes i_r)=1$ and $t_{a,r}s_{a,r}=h_*(1\otimes h^*p_r)t_{a,N_r}q_{a,N_r}h_*(1\otimes h^*i_r)=1$. These are actual equations of module-sheaf maps, not equations of derived morphisms being promoted to chain equalities. The termwise counit and its naturality are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy]; the inverse formula is the one in [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows].

proof.text: For any map $u:F^r\to F^{r+1}$, naturality of $t$ gives $B(u)t_r=t_{r+1}A(u)$, where $A(u)=1\otimes u$ and $B(u)=h_*(1\otimes h^*u)$. Multiply on the left by $s_{r+1}$ and on the right by $s_r$ to obtain $s_{r+1}B(u)=A(u)s_r$. For a map $w:I^a\to I^{a+1}$, put $A(w)=h_*w\otimes1$ and $B(w)=h_*(w\otimes1)$. Counit naturality gives $B(w)t_{a,r}=t_{a+1,r}A(w)$. Composing on the left with $s_{a+1,r}$ and on the right with $s_{a,r}$ gives $s_{a+1,r}B(w)=A(w)s_{a,r}$. Apply these identities to $d_F$ and $d_I$. Thus both families commute with both bicomplex differentials; no compatibility of the chosen splittings with $d_F$ is required. This uses the natural termwise counit of [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] and the inverse equations just computed.

proof.text: Use the tensor-total differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. On the summand $(a,r)$ it is $d_I\otimes1+(-1)^a1\otimes d_F$. Since $t_{a,r}$ and $s_{a,r}$ preserve both indices, the horizontal identity carries coefficient $1$ on both sides and the vertical identity carries the same coefficient $(-1)^a$ on both sides. Add the two commuting squares to obtain $dt=td$ and $ds=sd$. Extend the maps over the finite direct sum in each total degree. Restriction to each summand gives $st=1$ and $ts=1$ by Step 2, hence these are equalities of total chain maps by the universal property of the direct sum. This proves inverse chain maps $t:C\to B$ and $s:B\to C$.

source.place: Proof, paragraphs 1 and 2 (expanded representative and sign argument)

proof.text: It remains to identify these maps with the arrows in the statement. Choose a K-flat resolution with flat terms $v:P\to A$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The complex $P\otimes F$ is K-flat directly from [def-pc-kflat-complex]: for an acyclic $Z$, reassociating the total tensor identifies $Z\otimes(P\otimes F)$ with $(Z\otimes P)\otimes F$; the first tensor is acyclic by K-flatness of $P$ and the second by K-flatness of $F$. Reassociation is the summandwise ordinary tensor associator with indices $(a,b,r)$, and the signs are $1,(-1)^a,(-1)^{a+b}$ on both sides, using [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Each term of $P\otimes F$ is a finite sum of retracts of finite sums of flat terms of $P$, hence flat. Tensor with $F$ and pull back: the ordinary pullback-tensor identification written in Step 2 identifies $h^*(P\otimes F)$ with $h^*P\otimes h^*F$; its localization is the canonical comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], and this computes $Lh^*(Rh_*E\otimes^L F)$. Under [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general], the localized map $Q(t\circ(v\otimes1))$ has adjunct the localization of $h^*P\otimes h^*F\xrightarrow{h^*v\otimes1}h^*h_*I\otimes h^*F\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_I\otimes1}I\otimes h^*F$. Indeed take its right-resolution arrow $s$ and left-resolution arrow $t$ in that node's representative formula to be identities at the chosen K-injective target $J$ and K-flat source $P\otimes F$; the representing comparison maps are the canonical derived ones. The first factor $h^*P\to I$ is, by the same formula applied to $Qv:QP\to Qh_*I=Rh_*E$, the derived counit at $E$ after its source comparison. Hence this adjunct is exactly $\varepsilon_E\otimes1$ after the derived pullback-tensor comparison. The defining adjunction in [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows] gives $Qt=\pi_{h,E,F}$. At each coefficient term the localized finite-free inverse used in Step 2 is the $\rho_r$ of that definition, so its summand formula gives $Qs_r=\rho_{F^r}$; [lemma-weil-pbc-projection-formula-projective-summand] confirms that this is the intrinsic inverse independent of presentation. The finite total map $Qs$ is therefore the specified $\rho_{h,E,F}$. Localization preserves compositions and identities, so the two equations of Step 4 become $\rho_{h,E,F}\pi_{h,E,F}=1$ and $\pi_{h,E,F}\rho_{h,E,F}=1$.
